title: Demo the autoSQL UI end-to-end against a seeded fake-data database
spec:
GATE ON INTEGRATION (Evan, 2026-08-19, verbatim): "we're going to need to see the SQL UI before we ever integrate this back into the GIMS, so make sure that demo with a database of fake information is on the todo list".

WHAT: a runnable, watchable demo of the autoSQL interactive UI — pick the data, pick how to view/window/transform it, and watch the tool generate the SQL underneath — driven end-to-end against a Postgres database seeded with synthetic (fake) records. Not slides, not a mockup: the real UI over a real database, launchable on this machine.

WHY IT EXISTS: autoSQL's whole premise is that a human picks the view/transform and the tool writes the SQL. That premise is unfalsifiable until someone WATCHES it happen. Evan has placed this as a hard prerequisite: autoSQL does not get integrated back into GIMS until the UI has been seen working. It is also the natural counterweight to the project's core risk — a SQL generator fails silently with subtly-wrong numbers (the reason this shop runs preset solo-builder-review with eyes before ship). A demo where the generated SQL is VISIBLE next to its result is how that failure mode gets caught by a human eye.

MUST INCLUDE:
1. A seeded database of fake information — synthetic, self-contained, regenerable by a committed script, no GIMS production data and no dependency on either GIMS tree being present. Shaped like the data autoSQL is meant for (GIMS-style arbitrary-key JSONB records, including the heartbeat/firehose shape that motivated the project).
2. The interactive UI: choose a source, choose a view/window/transform, see the result.
3. The generated SQL shown to the user alongside the result — the demo's whole point is that the SQL is inspectable, not hidden.
4. A do-X-expect-Y walkthrough so Evan can drive it himself and check the numbers, not just watch a recording.
5. One command to launch it from a clean checkout.

OUT OF SCOPE: integrating into GIMS (that is what this demo gates), production data, auth, deployment.

DEPENDS ON: the expression/compiler layer T-1 is currently spiking. T-1 recommends NO-GO on the standalone-compiler-plus-thin-adapter architecture as scoped; this ticket must be re-read against whatever Evan decides at T-1's sp_decide gate, because the demo's SQL-generation layer is exactly what that decision governs. Do not start building until sp_decide is cleared.

Worse, the new guard test parametrizes only the six holder-type shapes round 1 already named, so it passes green while these still 500 - the same structural test-blindness round 1 flagged for the AC-32 guard, reproduced inside the test written to close it. (2) LOW/latent - the serving-layer font strip only matches the canonical route spelling; dot-segment, doubled-slash and trailing-slash paths fall through to the raw mount and serve the live googleapis @import. Not a live AC-32 breach (the page links canonically and browsers normalise) but the stated guarantee is false. Everything else in the fix diff verified sound, including the ordering fix end-to-end, both named refusals, the read-only guard's rollback subtlety, CSS digest integrity and the run-demo shell's quoting. Full report: .autodev/specs/T-2-review-round-2.md · leaving: Machine review: code review + security review + full preflight (lint, typecheck, unit,… · next: Implement the plan: code + tests on the ticket branch.

history.by: agent:claude(on-behalf:evan,GA-6):auto-review round 1: 16 confirmed defects, 4 HIGH. Four lenses reviewed the diff and every finding was then handed to a separate agent whose job was to REFUTE it, defaulting to not-real when uncertain; 16 survived that and 1 did not. The headline finding inverts the demo's own signal: Postgres sorts a top-level empty jsonb array below everything including null, the spec's ordering table omits that exception, so a UI-reachable pick makes the red disagreement banner fire when the generated SQL is RIGHT and the independent Python control is WRONG - and the suite pins the wrong value. Also: the served page fetches a stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com on every load while the AC-32 test guarding 'no network' reads only two files that never contained the URL; run-demo's readiness poll is a second unfenced connection factory that PGHOSTADDR can redirect off 127.0.0.1; and every aggregated value in all 568 tests is a small integer, so a float-contaminated aggregate passes the whole suite.
